name: Adam Garcia

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, an independent group. We have no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, political parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about a usual shift.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I’m 43 and lead the account and delivery calls at our contact centre. My two-year college diploma got me in, but I became good by tracing the small errors that send a customer around three teams. I earn at the high end for this work. I use the approved AI assistant daily to search old cases, then check its answer against the live account.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What part of that day stays with you after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Elise repairs buses, and our two children are in school. We have a mortgage and about eleven months of expenses saved. Several other centres are close enough to reach after school drop-off. I like teaching an agent to find the actual charge; I am less pleased when a quick AI reply counts as a solved case.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell my team AI Plateau looks like our current case search with a few better shortcuts. I would still ask agents to check the charge before saying a refund is done.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead shift stays busy. With eleven months saved and other centres nearby, the mortgage is not in danger from a small efficiency change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading account calls and compare the assistant’s suggested refund date with the ledger on ten closed cases. In the first year of this mild change, I’d show any wrong dates to the quality lead during paid work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm, mostly. A quick search is useful when it does not turn a pending refund into a false promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What error did you catch?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Yesterday the assistant found the right customer but the wrong transaction on the same page. I spotted it because the payment amount differed by one digit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use the reserve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would leave our eleven-month reserve for the mortgage and unexpected repairs. Elise (my partner) and I have no reason to spend it just because the tool saves a minute.

say: I’d say **AI case search** saves time when agents check the ledger.
I’d show **wrong refund dates** to the quality lead.
think: I think my **lead shift** remains busy with small shortcuts.
I trust our **eleven-month reserve** against an ordinary disruption.
do: Keep **leading account calls** and compare ten AI refund dates with ledgers in 2026.
Show **wrong dates** during paid quality work in the first year.
feel: **Calm**, with attention to false refund promises.
S0.quote: A quick search is useful when it does not turn a pending refund into a false promise.
fieldNote: He already uses **AI daily** for searching but checks live records.
The **one-digit error** shows why he distrusts a fast summary.
He retains the **existing reserve** without claiming new saving.

steps.text: Keep leading account calls and check ten AI refund dates against ledgers

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues Steady Disruption will absorb the easy delivery messages and expose us to harder complaints. I would ask agents to join me in requesting paid correction time and a written evening rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can lead the difficult queue, but fewer paid seats could reduce my hours. Eleven months saved gives Elise and me time to compare offers, not a reason to accept a hollow title.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d learn the new AI exception screen by testing twenty old delivery disputes on a paid shift and comparing each proposed closure with the ledger. We would submit a joint paid-hours request. In the first year routine messages move, I’d apply to a posted paid claims desk only with written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and school care, and keep my present job until a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the paid rota, interested in the test. I want to see the error rate before anyone removes an agent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which exceptions would you test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would include cases where a driver marked a delivery complete while the refund remained pending. The exception screen ought to show both dates.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would a new rota fit home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elise (my partner) works early shifts, so I would check which of us could collect the children. A higher rate can disappear into after-school care.

say: I’d ask agents together for **paid correction time** and written hours.
I’d share **exception-screen errors** from tested delivery disputes.
think: I think I could lead the **harder complaint queue**.
I fear **fewer paid seats** would cut my hours despite savings.
do: Learn the **new AI screen** through twenty paid-shift delivery tests in 2026.
Join agents’ **written paid-hours request** after checking the errors.
Apply for **posted paid claims work** only with written mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel and school care; keep current work until signing.
feel: **Anxious** about hours, curious about the test.
S1.quote: I want to see the error rate before anyone removes an agent.
fieldNote: His **new AI learning** goes beyond daily case search.
A **joint worker demand** follows the paid-shift error test.
The offer needs **net weekly pay** after travel and school care.

steps.text: Learn new AI exception screen by testing twenty old delivery disputes on paid time
Join agents requesting written paid correction hours
Apply for posted claims with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and pickup; keep current job until signing

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2028 could settle the whole delivery complaint, including the check I do best. Robots around 2031 are later; the headset could stop paying first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think my lead post may vanish quickly. Eleven months saved and nearby centres make a search possible, but those centres may face the same cheap thinking AI.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d ask management for written staffing dates and join the agents asking for a paid human appeal when AGI gets a charge wrong. If my hours end in the first year after 2028, I’d apply for a posted paid transport-claims role only with written weekly wages and hours covering our mortgage after travel and childcare; I would not resign before a signed offer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed for the floor, anxious for our own income. Eleven months saved is a search window, not a replacement career.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would handle a wrong charge?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask who can reverse a wrong fare decision after AGI closes a case. If the appeal person cannot edit the account, the customer is still stuck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the new rota workable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elise (my partner) and I would compare the transport office’s rota with her bus-repair shifts. We would reject a job if its late hours required care that wiped out the extra wage.

say: I’d demand **written staffing dates** for the paid evening queue before 2028.
I’d demand a **paid human appeal** with correction authority.
think: I think my **lead post** could disappear quickly even after years of good work.
I doubt **nearby centres** escape the same AGI pressure.
do: Request **staffing dates** and join agents’ paid-appeal demand in 2026.
Apply after hours end for **posted paid transport claims** with written mortgage-covering wages/hours after travel/childcare; leave after signing an offer.
Compare **Elise’s bus-repair rota** and school pickup before accepting, rejecting care costs that wipe out extra wages.
feel: **Alarmed** for coworkers, anxious about household income.
S2.quote: Eleven months saved is a search window, not a replacement career.
fieldNote: His **eleven-month cushion** buys search time but cannot replace a lasting weekly wage.
The appeal request demands **correction authority** for wrong fares.

steps.text: Join agents requesting written staffing dates and paid appeals with correction authority
Apply after hours end for posted transport claims with written net mortgage-covering wages/hours; leave after signing
Compare Elise’s bus-repair rota, school pickup and care costs before accepting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AGI by 2031 gives us time to see whether a new claims desk is real work. I would ask the union delegates to press for paid trial shifts, not just training links.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I could learn transport claims before 2031, but general AI may eventually check fares too. I would only leave my current wage for a real position with authority to correct a charge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d join the delegates’ request and take a supervised paid trial at a transport-claims desk only if it posts a paid opening. If the opening requires a records course, I’d take it only with employer-funded fees and paid study hours. In the first year after 2031 I’d move only on a signed offer with written weekly pay and hours covering the mortgage after travel and childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy, with enough time to try a shift. I can learn a new ledger more easily than I can replace a lost weekly wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the trial involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would trace a disputed fare from the card tap to the corrected charge with a supervisor beside me. If the desk can only send another message, I would stay with calls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the trial cost the family?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elise (my partner) would compare my trial hours with the school pickup. The trial must be paid or we would be using our savings to subsidise the office.

say: I’d ask delegates for **paid trial shifts** at a posted claims desk.
I’d insist on **correction authority** in any new role.
think: I think I could learn a **transport ledger** before 2031.
I know **AGI may check fares** in that role too.
do: Join **delegates’ paid-trial request**; try supervised claims work only for a posted paid opening and paid trial hours fitting pickup.
Take **required records training** only with employer-funded fees and paid hours for that vacancy.
Move after 2031 only on a **signed written offer** with correction authority and weekly wages/hours covering mortgage after travel and childcare.
feel: **Uneasy**, with time to test a paid shift.
S3.quote: I can learn a new ledger more easily than I can replace a lost weekly wage.
fieldNote: The **trial must be paid** and tied to a posted opening.
A required course needs **funded fees** and paid study time.
The signed offer must cover **travel and childcare** before moving.

steps.text: Join delegates requesting paid trial shifts for posted claims openings
Try supervised paid claims shift only for a posted paid opening fitting school pickup
Take vacancy-required records course only with employer-funded fees and paid study hours
Move only on signed written net mortgage-covering wages/hours and correction authority after comparing pickup

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell colleagues AGI by 2036 gives us a decade to get paid appeals and proper trial shifts into the contract. I would keep bringing real correction cases to our union meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I think I can earn my higher wage and keep our eleven-month reserve for many years. Full thinking AI may still reach the account desk in 2036, while robots around 2039 come later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: In 2026 I’d keep leading the account queue and join our annual request for paid correction hours. In the first year after 2036, if my hours fall, I’d move to a posted paid account-review job only on signed written weekly wages and hours covering the mortgage after travel and childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the later end, steady enough to plan today. Ten years can keep a family earning, but only if the paid hours stay real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union meeting see?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would bring the number of overturned charges to the meeting beside the paid appeal hours. That makes the request about customer harm and staffing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the family move?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Elise (my partner) and I would keep the children at their school unless a signed job offer covered our mortgage after extra travel and housing costs. Plenty of local centres mean we can look without moving home first.

I’d seek **paid appeal hours** and trial shifts in the contract.
think: I think I can **keep earning** and retain our existing reserve.
I know **2036 AGI** may still take the account desk.
do: Keep **leading account calls** and join annual requests for paid correction hours.

S4.quote: Ten years can keep a family earning, but only if the paid hours stay real.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could do both my call and my account check. Eleven months saved gives us room to search, but I want written staffing notice and a paid way for customers to challenge a wrong decision. A posted job with written whole-week pay and a workable school rota would matter more than a course promise.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask the customer what a correction costs them while it waits. A disputed bus pass charge can keep a customer’s child from travelling to school the next morning.

headlineQuote: A disputed bus pass charge can keep a customer’s child from travelling to school the next morning.
portrait: At **43**, Adam is a top-skilled contact-centre lead with a two-year diploma and higher pay.
He and Elise have **two schoolchildren**, a mortgage and about eleven months of expenses saved.
He uses **AI daily** to search cases but checks live account records.
He values **paid appeals** and tests new tools before considering posted work nearby.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could take both his customer calls and account checks.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a paid appeal route and posted work with reliable family-compatible pay would help.
